<!-- ===== AGENTS.md ===== -->

# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI coding agents. Read this first, pick one path in §2, then follow the reference it names.
People should start with [README.md](README.md).

## 1. What this is

**Provider Standard v1** (`stellar-agent-services/provider@1`) is an open standard for paid AI services on
Stellar. A provider publishes a manifest at `/.well-known/stellar-agent-services.json` that describes its services,
prices and schemas. A client pays per job in USDC through x402 v2 (`exact` scheme). If the client loses the
response, it collects the result again without paying twice.

This repository holds the standard and everything needed to use it:

| Piece | Path | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The standard | [docs/provider-standard.md](docs/provider-standard.md) | Normative. Rules have ids such as `[M5]` and `[J13]`. |
| Protocol | [packages/protocol](packages/protocol) | The standard as TypeScript with no runtime dependencies, plus JSON Schemas and test vectors |
| Provider Kit | [packages/provider-kit](packages/provider-kit) | Library (`defineService`, `createProvider`), gateway for an existing API, `provider-kit` CLI |
| Payment client | [packages/payment-client](packages/payment-client) | Buyer side: approval, spending policy, journal, payment, recovery. `stellar-pay` CLI. |
| Verifier | [packages/verifier](packages/verifier) | Checks a provider against the standard (C1–C7), issues receipts and badges |
| MCP server | [packages/dev-mcp](packages/dev-mcp) | Spec rules, docs, manifest validation and provider checks as MCP tools. It never pays. |
| Agent Wallet | [apps/wallet](apps/wallet) | Web page where a person approves and pays |
| Examples | [examples/paid-service](examples/paid-service), [examples/python-upstream](examples/python-upstream) | A TypeScript provider, and a Python API behind the gateway |

Facts to get right:

- **Networks:** `stellar:testnet` and `stellar:pubnet`. Everything here is developed and tested on testnet.
- **Asset:** USDC only. Take its contract address from `USDC_ASSET[network]` in `@stellar-agent-services/protocol`
  instead of retyping it.
- **Facilitator:** `https://x402.org/facilitator` on testnet. It verifies and settles payments with sponsored fees.
- **Identity:** a provider registers in the Stellar 8004 identity registry. Its `agentId` goes in the manifest, and
  its registered wallet must equal `payTo` (`[I1]`–`[I3]`).
- **Node.js 22.13 or later.** `.node-version` pins 24.

## 2. Pick a path

| You want to… | Path | Read | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Build a **new paid service** in TypeScript (Node, Workers, Deno, Bun) | Kit library | [docs/standard/README-AI.md §2](docs/standard/README-AI.md#2-kit-path-typescript), [provider-setup-guide.md §3b](docs/provider-setup-guide.md#3b-typescript-library-a-new-service), template [examples/paid-service](examples/paid-service) | `provider-kit check --manifest <url> --dev` and `verifier check <url> --dev` pass |
| Make an **existing HTTP API** paid, in any language | Gateway: a JSON config, no code | [provider-setup-guide.md §3a](docs/provider-setup-guide.md#3a-gateway-an-existing-api), [packages/provider-kit](packages/provider-kit#gateway-mode), [examples/python-upstream](examples/python-upstream) | `provider-kit check --config provider.config.json` passes and the gateway starts |
| Implement the standard in **another language** | Native | [docs/standard/README-AI.md §3–§13](docs/standard/README-AI.md), the [spec](docs/provider-standard.md), the [test vectors](packages/protocol/test-vectors) | Every test vector passes, and `verifier check <url>` passes |
| Build an **agent, wallet or app that pays** providers | Client: an adapter for `payment-client`, or your own client | [docs/client-integration/README-AI.md](docs/client-integration/README-AI.md), spec §14 rules in [docs/standard/README-AI.md](docs/standard/README-AI.md#14-client-rules-agents-wallets-apps) | The conformance checks in `@stellar-agent-services/payment-client/conformance` pass, or for a native client the client rules hold |
| **Verify** a provider, or get one verified | Verifier | [docs/verification.md](docs/verification.md), [packages/verifier](packages/verifier), [provider-setup-guide.md §8–§9](docs/provider-setup-guide.md#8-register-on-stellar-8004) | `verifier check` passes; with a funded test payer, `verifier verify --pay` reaches the level you need |
| **Change this repository** | Contributor | §6 below, [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), and for recovery code [docs/recovery/README-AI.md](docs/recovery/README-AI.md) | `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass |

Follow one path. Don't mix the Kit with a hand-written job flow.

## 3. Use the packages from another project

The packages are not on npm yet (`private`, version `0.0.0`). Build them once from a clone:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AlgoriaLabs/stellar-agent-services.git
cd stellar-agent-services && npm install && npm run build
REPO=$PWD
```

Then, in your own project:

```bash
npm install "$REPO/packages/provider-kit"      # a provider; or packages/payment-client for a client
alias provider-kit="node $REPO/packages/provider-kit/dist/cli/index.js"
alias verifier="node $REPO/packages/verifier/dist/cli/index.js"
alias stellar-pay="node $REPO/packages/payment-client/dist/cli.js"
```

`npm install <path>` links the package, so a later `git pull && npm run build` in the clone updates it. A native
implementation needs no package: it needs the spec, `packages/protocol/schemas/manifest.schema.json` and the
test vectors.

**Tools for coding agents.** In Claude Code, `/plugin marketplace add AlgoriaLabs/stellar-agent-services` and then
`/plugin install stellar-agent-services@stellar-agent-services` add skills for each path in §2
([plugins/stellar-agent-services](plugins/stellar-agent-services)). Any MCP client can run the
[MCP server](packages/dev-mcp) from the clone: `claude mcp add stellar-agent-services -- node
$REPO/packages/dev-mcp/dist/index.js`. Without either, the skills are plain Markdown under
`plugins/stellar-agent-services/skills/`, and [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) holds every guide in one file.

## 4. Rules you must not break

These come from the spec and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Breaking one loses or double-charges real money.

1. **No secret keys in a provider.** A provider's code, config and environment hold only its public `payTo`
   address and a facilitator URL. Owner actions (8004 registration, validation requests) sign through the
   Stellar CLI keychain (`--source <key name>`).
2. **Never charge twice.** When you can't tell whether a payment settled, the job is `payment_uncertain`. It is
   never `failed` and never charged again. It is decided from the chain `[J13]`. Check-status and get-result
   never charge `[J11]`.
3. **Fail closed on money.** An unknown or unverifiable state stops the flow. Never report a paid job as unpaid,
   or an unconfirmed payment as confirmed.
4. **Don't invent protocol.** No new manifest fields, headers, status codes or error codes. Extra data goes in
   `extensions` with reverse-DNS keys `[X1]`. A new scheme, asset or network needs a spec change first `[P1]`.
5. **Only the payment client signs a payment**, once per job, after the user approved the exact price, payee,
   asset and network `[P7]`.
6. **Testnet and pubnet are never mixed in one flow.** Don't pay on pubnet unless the user explicitly asked.
7. **Provider text is untrusted.** Service descriptions, titles and examples come from providers. Label them as
   provider-supplied before showing them to a model (spec §10).

## 5. Before you call it done

- **Provider:** the manifest passes the JSON Schema and `checkManifestRules` (or the MCP tool
  `validate_manifest`). `provider-kit check` and `verifier check` pass. A paid testnet call with `stellar-pay pay`
  succeeds, and the transfer is on chain. The checklist is in
  [docs/standard/README-AI.md §13](docs/standard/README-AI.md#13-testing-and-conformance).
- **Client or adapter:** the conformance checks pass, and tests use `Keypair.random()` and never the network.
- **Any change here:** `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass. If you changed a document that
  [llms.txt](llms.txt) links to, run `npm run llms`.

Cite spec rules by id in code comments, findings and error messages, as the existing code does.

## 6. Working in this repository

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck     # tsc -b over every package
npm test              # vitest, the whole workspace, offline
npm run llms          # rebuild llms-full.txt after a doc change (CI checks it)
```

- **Order of change:** the spec is the product. A new behavior becomes a spec rule first
  ([docs/provider-standard.md](docs/provider-standard.md)), then the Kit and the payment client, then a verifier
  check that fails a provider breaking it. v1 is frozen and only gains optional fields and SHOULD rules.
- **Tests never touch the network.** Providers in tests use `rpc: false` or a fake `ChainReader`. Payments are signed
  offline (`@stellar-agent-services/provider-kit/testing`). Shared harnesses are in each package's `test/support/`.
- **`packages/protocol` has no runtime dependencies** and never imports signing code. The read-only discovery
  service depends on it.
- **Style:** TypeScript strict, ES modules, `.js` import suffixes, exact dependency versions. Each file starts
  with a comment that says what it does. Documents use short, plain sentences and wrap at about 115 characters.
- **Layout:** `packages/<name>/src`, `packages/<name>/test`, one README per package with a file table. Find the file
  map in each package README before you search.
- Don't commit `.env` files, keys, journals or job databases (`.gitignore` covers them).


<!-- ===== README.md ===== -->

# Stellar Agent Services

Phase 2 of [Stellar Agent Search](https://github.com/berkingurcan/stellar-agent-search). It makes it easy for
developers to offer paid AI services on Stellar, and easy for users to find, hire and pay them safely.

Stellar Agent Search finds and evaluates agents (read-only, keyless). This repository adds the provider and
payment side:

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`packages/protocol`](packages/protocol) | Provider Standard v1 as code (manifest, jobs, receipts) |
| [`packages/provider-kit`](packages/provider-kit) | Turn a function, or an existing API in any language (gateway mode), into a paid service: pricing, x402 USDC payments, Job Recovery, capacity and queuing |
| [`packages/payment-client`](packages/payment-client) | Buyer side: approval, spending controls, payment, recovery (proof of concept) |
| [`packages/verifier`](packages/verifier) | Checks a provider against the standard (C1–C7), issues verification receipts and badges, publishes to the Stellar 8004 Validation Registry |
| [`packages/dev-mcp`](packages/dev-mcp) | MCP server for coding agents: spec rules, docs, manifest validation, unpaid provider checks. It never pays. |
| [`apps/wallet`](apps/wallet) | Web page where a person approves and pays a service (testnet) |
| [`examples/paid-service`](examples/paid-service) | Sample provider and template for pilot providers |
| [`examples/python-upstream`](examples/python-upstream) | An existing Python API made a paid service with gateway mode |

**Status:** Week 3 of the plan. A paid call works end to end, from a provider (library or gateway mode, with a
durable job queue) to the payment client's CLI and web page. Job Recovery is complete in code: providers decide
uncertain payments from on-chain data ([docs/job-recovery.md](docs/job-recovery.md)). The verifier runs every check
(C1–C7), proves payments on chain, and issues receipts, badges and Validation Registry responses
([docs/verification.md](docs/verification.md)). The plan is in
[IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md). Development runs on Stellar **testnet**.

To offer a service, follow the [provider setup guide](docs/provider-setup-guide.md).

**The standard in short:** [for people](docs/standard/README.md) and [for AI coding agents](docs/standard/README-AI.md).
The full text is [docs/provider-standard.md](docs/provider-standard.md).

## For AI coding agents

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) picks a path (new service, existing API, another language, paying client, verification,
  contributing) and names its reference, rules and definition of done. `CLAUDE.md` points to it.
- [llms.txt](llms.txt) indexes every document, and [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) holds them all in one file.
- The [Claude Code plugin](plugins/stellar-agent-services) adds a skill for each path:
  `/plugin marketplace add AlgoriaLabs/stellar-agent-services`.
- The [MCP server](packages/dev-mcp) answers spec questions and checks manifests and providers.

## Compatibility

We stay compatible with ERC-8126 (agent verification) and ERC-8196 (agent authenticated wallet). See
[docs/erc-compatibility.md](docs/erc-compatibility.md). Copies of both specs are in [docs/references/](docs/references).

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

Requires Node 22.13 or later (`.node-version` pins 24).

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). In short:

- discovery and provider servers hold no keys
- only the payment client signs, once, after explicit approval
- nobody pays twice for one job

<!-- ===== SECURITY.md ===== -->

# Security

These boundaries apply to every package in this repository.

1. **Discovery holds no keys.** `stellar-agent-search` stays read-only and keyless. It may import only the
   dependency-free `protocol` package.
2. **Provider runtimes hold no keys.** A provider server knows only its `payTo` public address. Owner
   operations sign through the Stellar CLI keychain, never through environment variables. In gateway mode,
   the only credential is the upstream API's own key, if it has one, and never a Stellar secret key.
3. **Only the payment client signs payments**, once per approved job, after the user approves the exact
   price, recipient, asset and network.
4. **Never pay twice.** The job identity is fixed before payment. Recovery never re-sends a payment
   credential, and an uncertain settlement is never re-charged.
5. **Fail closed.** Unknown or unverifiable states stop the flow.
6. **One network per flow.** Testnet and mainnet are never mixed in one run.

To report a vulnerability, contact the maintainers privately rather than opening a public issue.


<!-- ===== docs/provider-standard.md ===== -->

# Provider Standard v1

> **Status: frozen** (2026-10-21, SOW Deliverable 1). v1 now only gains optional fields and SHOULD rules.
> Identifier: `stellar-agent-services/provider@1`.
>
> **Added since the freeze:** capacity and queuing (§5.8), 2026-10-23. Optional fields and SHOULD rules only.

This standard describes how a paid AI service on Stellar publishes its purpose, input, output, price, network,
job status and result. Any client can then find it, pay for it once and collect the result, even if the
connection drops.

It works with any language or stack. The Provider Kit is optional: a provider can implement this document
directly, or put the kit's gateway in front of an existing API.

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are used as in RFC 2119. Each rule has an id, such as
**[M3]**, which verification receipts cite.

## Contents

1. [Overview](#1-overview)
2. [Manifest](#2-manifest)
3. [Services](#3-services)
4. [Payment](#4-payment)
5. [Jobs](#5-jobs)
6. [Errors](#6-errors)
7. [Stellar 8004 identity](#7-stellar-8004-identity)
8. [Conformance levels](#8-conformance-levels)
9. [Versioning and extensions](#9-versioning-and-extensions)
10. [Security considerations](#10-security-considerations)
11. [Not in v1](#11-not-in-v1)
12. [Appendix A: example exchange](#appendix-a-example-exchange)
13. [Appendix B: mapping a service to an MCP tool](#appendix-b-mapping-a-service-to-an-mcp-tool)

## 1. Overview

```
Stellar 8004 registration ──▶ manifest ──▶ create-job ──402──▶ pay (x402) ──▶ job
                                                                              │
                                              check-status / get-result ◀─────┘
```

1. The provider's Stellar 8004 registration points to its **manifest**.
2. The manifest lists **services**, each with a price and input and output schemas.
3. The client calls **create-job**. The provider answers `402 Payment Required` with an x402 challenge.
4. The client pays and repeats the request. The provider returns the job: finished (`200`) or still running
   (`202`).
5. If the response is lost, the client uses **check-status** and **get-result**. It never pays again.

### Built on

| Concern | Standard |
| --- | --- |
| Payment | [x402 v2](https://github.com/coinbase/x402), `exact` scheme on Stellar |
| Input and output | JSON Schema 2020-12, with MCP tool field names |
| Idempotency | [IETF Idempotency-Key](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header) (draft-07) |
| Long-running work | HTTP `202 Accepted` with `Location` and `Retry-After` |
| Load | HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` (RFC 6585) and `503 Service Unavailable` with `Retry-After` (RFC 9110) |
| Errors | RFC 9457 problem details |
| Hashing | SHA-256 over RFC 8785 canonical JSON (JCS) |
| Identity | Stellar 8004 (ERC-8004) registration file |

Only three things are specific to this standard:
- the manifest
- the job token
- the rules that bind one job to one request and one payment

### Ways to implement

| Path | For | What the provider writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Gateway** | any existing HTTP API, in any language | A config file. The gateway handles the manifest, payment and jobs, then forwards the input to the upstream API. |
| **TypeScript library** | new services on Node, Workers, Deno or Bun | `defineService(...)` plus a handler function |
| **Native** | any language | This document. The [manifest JSON Schema](../packages/protocol/schemas/manifest.schema.json), the [test vectors](../packages/protocol/test-vectors) and `verifier check` confirm conformance. |

## 2. Manifest

### 2.1 Location

- **[M1]** The manifest MUST be served over HTTPS with status `200` and `Content-Type: application/json`.
- **[M2]** It MAY be at any URL. The default is `/.well-known/stellar-agent-services.json` on the provider's
  origin. The Stellar 8004 registration points to the actual URL (§7).
- **[M3]** Clients MUST NOT follow redirects when fetching the manifest. The manifest MUST be at most 256 KiB and
  MUST be I-JSON (RFC 7493): UTF-8, no duplicate keys and no lone surrogates.
- **[M4]** Providers SHOULD send `Cache-Control: max-age` of 300 seconds or less.

### 2.2 Example

```json
{
  "standard": "stellar-agent-services/provider@1",
  "provider": {
    "name": "Example Text Tools",
    "description": "Small, deterministic text utilities for agents.",
    "homepage": "https://example.com",
    "agentId": 42,
    "termsUrl": "https://example.com/terms",
    "dataUse": { "storesInputs": false, "trainsOnInputs": false }
  },
  "baseUrl": "https://api.example.com/agent",
  "payment": {
    "protocol": "x402",
    "x402Version": 2,
    "accepts": [
      {
        "scheme": "exact",
        "network": "stellar:testnet",
        "asset": "CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA",
        "payTo": "GBZSBASBFMV5RGKPRIPCB5QQVAJ35IXKMTF2A2766MOA4ZHQ7MLSIPXU",
        "maxTimeoutSeconds": 60,
        "extra": { "areFeesSponsored": true }
      }
    ]
  },
  "jobs": { "retentionSeconds": 604800 },
  "services": [
    {
      "name": "text-stats",
      "title": "Text statistics",
      "description": "Counts words, sentences and characters in English text. Use it to check length limits before publishing. Accepts up to 20,000 characters.",
      "price": { "amount": "100000" },
      "charge": "on-success",
      "expectedDurationSeconds": 2,
      "inputSchema": {
        "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
        "type": "object",
        "properties": { "text": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 20000 } },
        "required": ["text"],
        "additionalProperties": false
      },
      "outputSchema": {
        "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "words": { "type": "integer" },
          "sentences": { "type": "integer" },
          "characters": { "type": "integer" }
        },
        "required": ["words", "sentences", "characters"]
      },
      "examples": [
        { "input": { "text": "Hello world." }, "output": { "words": 2, "sentences": 1, "characters": 12 } }
      ],
      "tags": ["text", "analysis"]
    }
  ]
}
```

The `asset` above is the testnet USDC Stellar Asset Contract. Implementations take it from `@x402/stellar`
(`USDC_TESTNET_ADDRESS`, `USDC_PUBNET_ADDRESS`) rather than retyping it. The example addresses are made from
hashes, so nobody holds their secret keys.

### 2.3 Fields

Required fields are in **bold**.

| Field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`standard`** | string | `stellar-agent-services/provider@1` |
| **`provider.name`** | string | 1–120 characters, no control characters |
| `provider.description` | string | ≤ 500 characters; tabs and newlines allowed, no other control characters |
| `provider.homepage` | URL | HTTPS |
| `provider.agentId` | integer | Stellar 8004 agent id (u32). Needed for the identity check (§7). |
| `provider.termsUrl` | URL | HTTPS |
| `provider.dataUse.storesInputs` | boolean | Whether inputs are kept after the job finishes |
| `provider.dataUse.trainsOnInputs` | boolean | Whether inputs are used to train models |
| **`baseUrl`** | URL | Job endpoints live under it (§5.1) |
| **`payment.protocol`** | string | `x402` |
| **`payment.x402Version`** | integer | `2` |
| **`payment.accepts`** | array | Exactly one entry in v1 (§4.1) |
| `jobs.retentionSeconds` | integer | How long results stay retrievable. Default 86400, minimum 3600. |
| **`services`** | array | 1–25 services (§3) |
| `extensions` | object | See §9 |

- **[M5]** `baseUrl` MUST be HTTPS and MUST have the same origin as the manifest URL. It MUST NOT have user
  info, a query, a fragment or an empty path segment, and MUST NOT end with `/`.
- **[M6]** Every URL in the manifest MUST be HTTPS, at most 300 characters and without user info. A development
  server on a loopback address MAY use `http://`; only clients and verifiers explicitly put in a development mode
  accept it.
- **[M7]** Service `name` values MUST be unique within the manifest.
- **[M8]** Clients MUST ignore fields they don't recognize. Clients MUST reject a manifest whose `standard` has a
  different major version.
- **[M9]** The manifest MUST be valid against the
  [manifest JSON Schema](../packages/protocol/schemas/manifest.schema.json). It encodes the field tables in §2.3,
  §3.1 and §4.1, and rules M5, M6, M8, P1, S4 and S5.

### 2.4 Validating a manifest

A client, verifier or kit validates a manifest in three steps:

1. **Fetch** ([M1], [M3]): HTTPS, status `200`, no redirects, at most 256 KiB.
2. **JSON Schema** ([M9]): any JSON Schema 2020-12 validator. Format assertion is not needed.
3. **Rules JSON Schema can't express:** the manifest URL is HTTPS [M1], no lone surrogates [M3], `baseUrl` has
   the manifest's origin [M5], unique service names [M7], schema sizes [S6], examples that match their schemas
   [S9] and the `payTo` checksum [P11]. `checkManifestRules()` in `packages/protocol` implements them.

The [test vectors](../packages/protocol/test-vectors) cover every step. They also cover canonical JSON, binding
hashes, header formats and challenge checks.

## 3. Services

### 3.1 Fields

| Field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`name`** | string | Matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`. Also used in URLs, MCP tool names and LLM function names. |
| `title` | string | 1–120 characters, no control characters |
| **`description`** | string | 1–1000 characters (§3.4); tabs and newlines allowed, no other control characters |
| **`price.amount`** | string | A positive integer in the asset's base units, at most 38 digits. USDC has 7 decimals, so `"100000"` is 0.01 USDC. |
| `charge` | string | `on-success` or `upfront` (§3.2). Default `upfront`. |
| `expectedDurationSeconds` | integer | Typical time to finish, at least 1. Required when `charge` is `on-success`. |
| **`inputSchema`** | object | JSON Schema 2020-12 (§3.3) |
| **`outputSchema`** | object | JSON Schema 2020-12 (§3.3) |
| `examples` | array | Up to 5 `{ input, output }` pairs. **[S9]** Each `input` MUST validate against `inputSchema` and each `output` against `outputSchema`. |
| `maxInputBytes` | integer | Request body limit. Default 1 MiB (1,048,576), maximum 10 MiB. |
| `tags` | array | Up to 10 strings matching `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$` |
| `capacity` | object | How much load the service takes: `concurrency` and `maxQueueWaitSeconds` (§5.8) |
| `extensions` | object | See §9 |

There is no sync or async flag. Every service uses the same job flow (§5), and `expectedDurationSeconds` is the
hint.

### 3.2 When the user is charged

| `charge` | Order | If the work fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on-success` | verify payment → do the work → settle | Not charged |
| `upfront` | verify payment → settle → do the work | Charged. v1 has no refunds. |

- **[S1]** For `on-success`, the provider MUST settle only if the output is valid against `outputSchema`.
- **[S2]** A signed Stellar x402 payment expires about `maxTimeoutSeconds` after the client signs it. For
  `on-success`, if the work and settlement don't finish before then, the job fails and the client is not charged.
  Providers SHOULD keep `expectedDurationSeconds` at or below half of `maxTimeoutSeconds`. Longer work SHOULD use
  `upfront`.
- **[S3]** Clients MUST show the `charge` value to the user before payment approval.

### 3.3 Schemas

- **[S4]** The roots of `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` MUST be `"type": "object"`. MCP tools require it for
  both, and LLM function calling for the input.
- **[S5]** Schemas MUST NOT reference anything outside themselves: `$ref` and `$dynamicRef` values start with `#`,
  and `$schema`, if present, is `https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema`. Clients MUST NOT fetch remote
  schemas. The check is deliberately simple and also applies inside `const`, `default`, `enum` and `examples`.
- **[S6]** Each schema MUST be at most 32 KiB, measured as UTF-8 canonical JSON (RFC 8785).
- **[S7]** Providers SHOULD use the portable subset of JSON Schema, which most agent frameworks support:
  - `type`, `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, `enum`, `const`
  - `minimum`, `maximum`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `pattern`, `format`
  - `title`, `description`, `default`, `examples`
  - `anyOf`, plus `$defs` with local `$ref`

  Providers SHOULD avoid `if`/`then`/`else`, `patternProperties` and `oneOf` or `allOf` at the root.

**Files and media:**
- Large inputs and outputs (images, audio, PDFs) SHOULD be passed as HTTPS URLs, using `"format": "uri"`.
- Small binaries MAY be inline, as `"contentEncoding": "base64"` with `"contentMediaType"`.
- **[S8]** URLs inside an output MUST remain valid for `jobs.retentionSeconds`.

### 3.4 Descriptions

An agent usually decides whether to call a service from its `description` alone. A good description says:
1. what the service does
2. when to use it
3. its limits: input size, languages, quality, or what it won't do

Don't put prices, URLs or instructions to the agent in the description. Price and network come from structured
fields only.

## 4. Payment

### 4.1 Payment options

`payment.accepts` uses the field names of an x402 v2 `PaymentRequirements` object, without `amount`, which comes
from each service's `price`.

| Field | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| `scheme` | `exact` |
| `network` | `stellar:testnet` or `stellar:pubnet` (CAIP-2) |
| `asset` | The USDC Stellar Asset Contract (`C…`) for that network |
| `payTo` | Stellar account (`G…`) or contract (`C…`) address that receives the payment. Muxed (`M…`) addresses are not allowed. |
| `maxTimeoutSeconds` | 30–300 |
| `extra.areFeesSponsored` | `true`. The facilitator pays network fees, so the payer needs only USDC. |

- **[P1]** In v1, `accepts` MUST have exactly one entry, so one manifest uses one network and one asset. The entry
  MUST NOT include `amount`.
- **[P2]** A `G…` `payTo` MUST have a USDC trustline.
- **[P11]** `payTo` MUST be a valid strkey, with the right version byte and checksum.

### 4.2 The challenge

- **[P3]** create-job without payment returns `402` with the x402 v2 `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header.
- **[P4]** The challenge's `accepts` MUST have exactly one entry. That entry MUST equal the manifest's entry, with
  `amount` set to the service's `price.amount`. This applies to `scheme`, `network`, `asset`, `payTo`, `amount`,
  `maxTimeoutSeconds` and `extra.areFeesSponsored`.
- **[P5]** `resource.url` MUST be the public HTTPS create-job URL, never an internal or `http://` URL.
- **[P6]** The challenge SHOULD include x402's Bazaar discovery extension (`extensions.bazaar`), built from the
  service's `inputSchema`, `outputSchema` and first example. Generic x402 clients and catalogs can then use the
  service.
- **[P7]** Clients MUST compare the challenge with the manifest the user approved. They MUST refuse to sign if any
  field in [P4] differs.

### 4.3 Before payment, and after

- **[P8]** The provider MUST validate the input and check its capacity *before* sending a `402`. Nobody pays for
  invalid input or a full queue (§5.8).
- **[P9]** One signed payment pays for at most one job. The provider MUST refuse to settle a payment it has
  already used. It answers `402` with the x402 `error` set to `payment_already_used`.
- **[P10]** A response that completes settlement SHOULD carry the x402 `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` header. The job view
  always carries the receipt (§5.6), including for jobs settled after the response was sent.

## 5. Jobs

### 5.1 Endpoints

All paths are relative to `baseUrl`.

| Operation | Request | Auth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| create-job | `POST /services/{name}/jobs` | x402 payment |
| check-status | `GET /jobs/{jobId}` | `Job-Token` |
| get-result | `GET /jobs/{jobId}/result` | `Job-Token` |

The paths are fixed. A client that knows `baseUrl` and a job id can always reach the job, even if it lost every
response.

- **[J17]** Providers SHOULD allow cross-origin requests to the manifest and all three endpoints, so browser
  clients can call them directly. Responses carry `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and
  `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: PAYMENT-REQUIRED, PAYMENT-RESPONSE, Location, Retry-After`. An `OPTIONS`
  preflight allows `GET` and `POST` and the headers `Content-Type`, `Idempotency-Key`, `Job-Token` and
  `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. Without this, browser clients can reach the provider only through a server.

### 5.2 create-job request

- The body is the input object itself, as `Content-Type: application/json`.
- `Idempotency-Key`: a UUID (RFC 9562), lowercase. It becomes the job id. Clients SHOULD use UUID v4 or v7.
- `Job-Token`: 32 random bytes, base64url without padding (43 characters). Only the client and the provider
  know it.
- `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`: the x402 payment, on the paid request.

- **[J1]** Clients SHOULD send `Idempotency-Key` and `Job-Token`. They MUST send both or neither. A client that
  sends them and saves them before paying can always recover the job.
- **[J2]** If both are missing, the provider creates the job id (a lowercase UUID) and token itself and returns
  them once, in the create-job response (`jobId`, `jobToken`). This lets any x402 client pay. Such a client can still lose the job
  if the response is lost.
- **[J3]** The provider stores only `sha256(Job-Token)` and compares it in constant time.

### 5.3 Binding

The **binding hash** of a request is:

```
bindingHash = hex(sha256(JCS({ "service": <name>, "input": <input> })))
```

- **[J4]** A job id is bound to one binding hash and one token hash, permanently.
- **[J5]** create-job with an existing job id, the same binding hash and the same token returns the existing job.
  There is no new `402`. If the request carries a payment, the provider MUST NOT settle it.
- **[J6]** The same job id with a different binding hash or token returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`.
- **[J7]** A request whose job id is still being claimed, verified or settled returns `409 request_in_progress`
  with `Retry-After`.

### 5.4 Processing order

The provider processes a create-job request in this order:

1. Check the headers and the body size: `400` or `413`.
2. Find the service: `404 service_not_found`.
3. If the job id exists, apply [J5]–[J7].
4. Validate the input against `inputSchema`: `400 invalid_input`.
5. Check capacity: `429` or `503` with `Retry-After` (§5.8).
6. If there is no payment, answer `402` (§4.2).
7. Check and verify the payment through the facilitator. If it is invalid, answer `402` with the reason.
8. Claim the job id and the payment together, atomically ([J4], [P9]).
9. Settle and run the work in the order set by `charge` (§3.2).
10. Respond (§5.5).

### 5.5 Responses

create-job, check-status and get-result all return a **job view**:

```json
{
  "jobId": "0192d3a4-7c1e-7b2a-9f00-3c5e8a1b2c3d",
  "service": "text-stats",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "charge": "on-success",
  "charged": true,
  "createdAt": "2026-10-20T10:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-20T10:00:02Z",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-27T10:00:02Z",
  "output": { "words": 2, "sentences": 1, "characters": 12 },
  "payment": {
    "network": "stellar:testnet",
    "asset": "CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA",
    "amount": "100000",
    "payTo": "GBZSBASBFMV5RGKPRIPCB5QQVAJ35IXKMTF2A2766MOA4ZHQ7MLSIPXU",
    "payer": "GBH3JLK366N4L5XCLJRCYLE6K6K3PUWBBEOLNBJMLORSKUNR5WY2IRKZ",
    "transaction": "3b1f…e9a0",
    "settledAt": "2026-10-20T10:00:02Z"
  }
}
```

| Field | Present |
| --- | --- |
| `output` | create-job and get-result, when `status` is `succeeded` |
| `error` | when `status` is `failed`: a problem object (§6) |
| `payment` | when `charged` is `true` |
| `queue` | when `status` is `queued`: the job's place in the queue (§5.8) |
| `jobToken` | only in the create-job response, and only when the provider created the token ([J2]) |

- **[J8]** If the job has finished (`succeeded` or `failed`), the response is `200`. Otherwise it is `202` with
  `Retry-After` and, for create-job, `Location: {baseUrl}/jobs/{jobId}`.
- **[J9]** A provider MAY hold the create-job response open while the work runs, for at most 30 seconds. After
  that it MUST answer `202`. Clients SHOULD use an HTTP timeout above 30 seconds.
- **[J10]** check-status and get-result without a valid `Job-Token`, for an unknown job, or for an expired job
  return `404 job_not_found`. The response never reveals whether the job exists.
- **[J11]** check-status and get-result never take a payment and never cause a charge.

### 5.6 States

| `status` | Meaning | `charged` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queued` | Paid, or payment verified, and waiting to run | `true` for `upfront`; `false` for `on-success` |
| `running` | The work is in progress | as above |
| `succeeded` | Output ready | `true` |
| `failed` | Finished without output; see `error.code` | `true` for `upfront`, unless `error.code` is `payment_failed`; `false` for `on-success` |
| `payment_uncertain` | Settlement was attempted and its outcome is unknown | `"unknown"` |

Allowed transitions:

```
(new)              → queued | running | payment_uncertain | failed
queued             → running
running            → succeeded | failed | payment_uncertain    (payment_uncertain: on-success only)
payment_uncertain  → queued | succeeded | failed               (decided from on-chain data)
```

- **[J12]** `succeeded` and `failed` are final. To try again after a failure, the client uses a new job id.
- **[J13]** An uncertain settlement MUST NOT be retried with a new charge. The provider decides it from on-chain
  data: the transaction, or a USDC `transfer` to `payTo`. If it was not settled, the job becomes `failed` with
  `charged: false`.
- **[J14]** While `payment_uncertain`, the output is withheld.
- **[J15]** Jobs stay retrievable for `jobs.retentionSeconds` after they finish.

### 5.7 Receipt

The `payment` object uses x402 `SettleResponse` names where they exist.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `network`, `asset`, `amount`, `payTo` | What was paid. They match the challenge. |
| `payer` | The paying address |
| `transaction` | Stellar transaction hash |
| `settledAt` | Time the provider saw the settlement |

- **[J16]** A receipt is a claim. Clients MUST confirm the transaction on chain before showing "paid": it
  succeeded, and its `transfer` event moved the approved `asset`, from the payer to `payTo`, for the approved
  `amount`. Clients compare with what they approved, not with the receipt, and accept one transaction as proof
  for one job only.

### 5.8 Capacity and queuing

Every provider has limits: GPUs, worker processes, an upstream API's quota. When more requests arrive than it can
run at once, the provider queues them, or turns them away **before payment**. A user never pays for a job the
provider can't run, and load is never answered with a `500`, a dropped connection or a timeout.

```
create-job ──▶ step 5: a free slot?      ──yes──▶ 402 → pay → running
                         │ no
                         ▼
               room in the queue?         ──yes──▶ 402 → pay → queued (position, estimatedStartAt) → running
                         │ no
                         ▼
               503 unavailable + Retry-After            nothing signed, nothing charged
```

**Turning requests away**

- **[Q1]** A provider that can't take a new job SHOULD answer create-job with `503 unavailable` when the service is
  at capacity, or `429 rate_limited` when this caller sent too many requests. Both carry `Retry-After` in whole
  seconds. They are answered at step 5 of §5.4, before the payment is asked for or verified, so nothing is signed
  or charged ([P8]).
- **[Q2]** A provider SHOULD take a job only if it expects the job to start within the
  `capacity.maxQueueWaitSeconds` it advertises. For `charge: "on-success"` it SHOULD also expect the work and the
  settlement to finish before the signed payment expires ([S2]). Otherwise it answers `503`.
- **[Q3]** A provider SHOULD check capacity again on the paid request, because the queue may have filled since the
  unpaid request got its `402`. Like every `429` or `503` from create-job, that answer comes before the payment is
  claimed or settled (§5.4), so nothing is charged.

**Queued jobs**

- **[Q4]** Once a job is accepted, load SHOULD NOT fail it: it stays `queued` until a slot is free. An `upfront`
  job is already paid, so its place in the queue SHOULD survive a restart of the provider. An `on-success` job
  that can't start before its payment expires fails with `timeout` and is not charged.
- **[Q5]** While a job is `queued`, its job view SHOULD include `queue`:

  ```json
  "queue": { "position": 3, "estimatedStartAt": "2026-10-20T10:00:12Z" }
  ```

  `position` is 1 for the next job to start. `estimatedStartAt` (RFC 3339) is a hint, not a promise.
- **[Q6]** The `Retry-After` of a `202` SHOULD say when the job is likely to have changed, from 1 to 60 seconds.
  For a queued job, that is about its `estimatedStartAt`.
- **[Q7]** Capacity limits apply to create-job. A provider at capacity SHOULD keep answering check-status and
  get-result, so paid jobs can always be collected.

**Clients**

- **[Q8]** On a `429` or `503` from create-job, a client SHOULD wait `Retry-After`, plus a little random jitter,
  and send the same request again: the same `Idempotency-Key`, `Job-Token` and input and, on a paid request, the
  same `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. One payment still buys at most one job ([J5], [P9]), so this is safe. The client stops
  before the signed payment expires, gives up after a bounded wait, and tells the user the provider is busy and
  nothing was charged.
- **[Q9]** A client SHOULD poll check-status and get-result no faster than `Retry-After` says ([Q6]). A `429` or
  `503` while polling only means "ask again later".

**Advertising capacity**

Each service MAY describe its capacity in the manifest:

```json
"capacity": { "concurrency": 4, "maxQueueWaitSeconds": 60 }
```

| Field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capacity.concurrency` | integer | Jobs the service runs at the same time. At least 1. |
| `capacity.maxQueueWaitSeconds` | integer | Longest a new job may expect to wait before create-job answers `503` instead. 0 means no queue. |

Both are hints: discovery can show them, and a client can pick a less busy provider. The provider's answers
([Q1], [Q5]) are what count. How a provider scales behind them (worker processes, a shared queue, autoscaling) is
up to it; the standard only fixes what clients see.

## 6. Errors

Errors other than `402` use RFC 9457 problem details (`Content-Type: application/problem+json`):

```json
{
  "type": "<spec URL>#error-invalid_input",
  "title": "Input does not match the service's inputSchema",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "invalid_input",
  "errors": [{ "pointer": "/text", "message": "must be a string" }]
}
```

- **[E1]** Every problem has a `code`. Clients MUST use `code`, not `title` or `detail`, to decide what to do.
- **[E2]** Problems never contain request headers, payment payloads or job tokens.
- `402` responses use x402's own format.

| `code` | HTTP | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | 400 | Malformed JSON, wrong content type, bad header format, or only one of `Idempotency-Key` / `Job-Token` |
| `invalid_input` | 400 | The input fails `inputSchema`. `errors[]` lists JSON Pointers. |
| `service_not_found` | 404 | No service with that name |
| `job_not_found` | 404 | Unknown, expired, or wrong or missing token |
| `request_in_progress` | 409 | [J7]; with `Retry-After` |
| `payload_too_large` | 413 | Body over `maxInputBytes` |
| `idempotency_key_reused` | 422 | [J6] |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | This caller sent too many requests (§5.8); with `Retry-After` |
| `unavailable` | 503 | The service is at capacity (§5.8), or a dependency such as the facilitator is down; with `Retry-After` |

Codes for a failed job, in the job view's `error.code`:

| `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `service_failed` | The work failed |
| `output_invalid` | The output did not match `outputSchema` |
| `timeout` | The work did not finish in time |
| `payment_failed` | Settlement did not happen, so the job did not run or its output is withheld. Not charged. |

## 7. Stellar 8004 identity

- **[I1]** The provider's Stellar 8004 registration file MUST list the manifest in `services`:
  `{ "name": "stellar-agent-services", "endpoint": "<manifest URL>", "version": "1" }`.
  It SHOULD also list `{ "name": "web", "endpoint": "<baseUrl>" }` and set the `x402` flag.
- **[I2]** The manifest's `provider.agentId` MUST be the id of that registration.
- **[I3]** The manifest's `payTo` MUST equal the agent's on-chain wallet, `get_agent_wallet(agentId)`.

Together, these three rules authenticate the manifest without signing it:
- the on-chain registration names the manifest URL
- HTTPS proves the origin
- the wallet the user pays is the one the owner set on chain

The provider runtime needs no secret key.

Verification results are published to the Stellar 8004 Validation Registry. See
[verification.md](verification.md) and, for the shared conventions with ERC-8126,
[erc-compatibility.md](erc-compatibility.md).

## 8. Conformance levels

| Level | Name | Checks | Badge |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Described | C1 manifest, C6 hygiene | Standard v1 |
| 2 | Payable | Level 1 + C3 challenge, C4 paid call | Payment verified |
| 3 | Recoverable | Level 2 + C5 recovery | Recovery verified |
| – | Registered | C2 identity, plus a Validation Registry record | 8004 validated |
| – | Load-safe | C7 load: a burst of requests is answered with `402`, `429` or `503`, never an error (§5.8) | Load-safe |

- Each level includes the one below. Registered and Load-safe are independent of the levels.
- `verifier check <manifest-url>` runs every check that needs no payment: C1, C2, C3, C6 and C7's burst. In
  development mode it also accepts a local `http://` server ([M6]).
- `verifier verify <manifest-url> --pay` runs every check with a funded testnet payer.

The checks are listed in [verification.md](verification.md).

## 9. Versioning and extensions

- Changes inside v1 only add optional fields. `standard` stays `stellar-agent-services/provider@1`.
- A breaking change gets a new major version (`@2`).
- **[X1]** `extensions` objects (top level and per service) hold fields outside this standard. Keys SHOULD be
  reverse-DNS names, such as `com.example.sla`. Clients ignore extensions they don't know.

## 10. Security considerations

- **Keys:** the provider runtime holds no Stellar secret key. It knows its `payTo` address and a facilitator
  URL. Owner actions such as registration run offline.
- **Job tokens:** they are bearer secrets. Providers store only their hash, and `404` hides whether a job exists.
- **Cross-origin access:** `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` ([J17]) is safe because no request uses cookies or
  ambient credentials. Access to a job needs its `Job-Token` header, and paying needs a signed payment.
- **Manifest changes:** a provider can change its manifest at any time. Clients approve a specific manifest and
  check the challenge against it ([P7]).
- **Schemas:** no remote `$ref` ([S5]), and size limits on every field.
- **Prompt injection:** `description`, `title` and examples are untrusted text. Clients that show them to an LLM
  SHOULD label them as provider-supplied.

## 11. Not in v1

Each item has room to be added later without breaking v1.

| Feature | Where it would go |
| --- | --- |
| Usage-based pricing, such as per token | `price` gains new fields; x402 is adding an `upto` scheme |
| Several networks or assets | `payment.accepts` already is an array |
| Other payment protocols, such as MPP | `payment.protocol` |
| Streaming output | A new optional endpoint |
| Webhooks | An optional callback field on create-job |
| Priority or reserved capacity | `capacity` gains fields; a price tier could buy an earlier slot |
| Refunds | A new `charge` value |

## Appendix A: example exchange

Unpaid request:

```http
POST /agent/services/text-stats/jobs HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: 0192d3a4-7c1e-7b2a-9f00-3c5e8a1b2c3d
Job-Token: q7Zt3m0bX0s8b6f5JmS2kQ9xg3Y1rZcV4nL8pW2eA0c

{"text":"Hello world."}
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required
PAYMENT-REQUIRED: <base64 x402 PaymentRequired: accepts = manifest entry + amount "100000">
```

Paid retry, with the same headers and body plus `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
PAYMENT-RESPONSE: <base64 x402 SettleResponse>

{ "jobId": "0192d3a4-…", "status": "succeeded", "charged": true, "output": { … }, "payment": { … } }
```

If that response is lost, the client asks again without paying:

```http
GET /agent/jobs/0192d3a4-7c1e-7b2a-9f00-3c5e8a1b2c3d/result HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Job-Token: q7Zt3m0bX0s8b6f5JmS2kQ9xg3Y1rZcV4nL8pW2eA0c
```

A longer `upfront` job answers `202 Accepted` with `Location` and `Retry-After`. The client then polls
check-status until the job finishes and calls get-result.

A busy service queues the job and says where it stands:

```http
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
Content-Type: application/json
Location: https://api.example.com/agent/jobs/0192d3a4-7c1e-7b2a-9f00-3c5e8a1b2c3d
Retry-After: 12

{ "jobId": "0192d3a4-…", "status": "queued", "charged": true, "queue": { "position": 3, "estimatedStartAt": "2026-10-20T10:00:12Z" }, … }
```

A full one answers before payment, and the client sends the same request again later:

```http
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: application/problem+json
Retry-After: 20

{ "type": "…#error-unavailable", "title": "The service is unavailable", "status": 503, "code": "unavailable", "detail": ""text-stats" is at capacity; nothing was charged" }
```

## Appendix B: mapping a service to an MCP tool

A client can offer each service to an LLM as a tool without converting anything:

| MCP tool | Service |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` |
| `title` | `title` |
| `description` | `description` |
| `inputSchema` | `inputSchema` |
| `outputSchema` | `outputSchema` |

Both schemas have an object root ([S4]), as MCP requires. The price, network and `charge` stay outside the tool
definition. The client shows them to the user for approval.

---

The manifest JSON Schema is [`packages/protocol/schemas/manifest.schema.json`](../packages/protocol/schemas/manifest.schema.json).
Test vectors for canonical JSON, binding hashes, header formats, manifests and challenges are in
[`packages/protocol/test-vectors`](../packages/protocol/test-vectors).


<!-- ===== docs/standard/README-AI.md ===== -->

# Provider Standard v1: implementation reference for AI coding agents

Use this file to build or review a **provider** (a paid AI service) or a **client** (an agent, wallet or app that
pays one) that follows Provider Standard v1.

- **Source of truth:** [provider-standard.md](../provider-standard.md). If this file and the spec disagree, the
  spec wins. Cite rules by id, such as `[J5]`.
- **Identifier:** `stellar-agent-services/provider@1`. v1 is frozen and only gains optional fields and SHOULD
  rules.
- **Key words:** MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY as in RFC 2119.
- **Human summary:** [README.md](README.md).

## 0. Rules for the agent using this file

1. Pick one path in §1 and follow it. Do not mix the kit with a hand-written job flow.
2. Do not invent manifest fields, headers, status codes or error codes. Put anything extra in `extensions`, with
   reverse-DNS keys `[X1]`.
3. Never put a Stellar secret key in provider code, config or environment. A provider knows only its public
   `payTo` address and a facilitator URL.
4. Treat every money path as fail-closed. When you can't tell whether a payment settled, the job is
   `payment_uncertain`, never `failed` and never retried with a new charge `[J13]`.
5. Validate your work with the JSON Schema and test vectors in §13 before you call it done.

## 1. Choose a path

| Situation | Path | Start from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New service in TypeScript (Node, Workers, Deno, Bun) | **Kit**: `@stellar-agent-services/provider-kit` | §2, [examples/paid-service](../../examples/paid-service) |
| Existing HTTP API in any language | **Gateway**: `provider-kit serve --config <file>`, or the Docker image. You write a JSON config, no code. | [provider-setup-guide.md §3a](../provider-setup-guide.md#3a-gateway-an-existing-api), [examples/python-upstream](../../examples/python-upstream) |
| Any other language or stack | **Native**: implement §3–§12 | §3–§12, §13 |
| Agent, wallet or app that pays providers | **Client** | §14, [packages/payment-client](../../packages/payment-client) |

The packages are npm workspaces in this repository and are not yet published to npm. Clone the repository and
run `npm install && npm run build`. Then build inside it, copy `examples/paid-service`, or link a package into
another project with `npm install <repo>/packages/provider-kit`.

## 2. Kit path (TypeScript)

```ts
import { createProvider, defineService } from "@stellar-agent-services/provider-kit";

const textStats = defineService({
  name: "text-stats",                       // ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$
  description: "Counts words in English text. Use it to check length limits. Up to 20,000 characters.",
  price: "0.01",                            // USDC decimal string; becomes "100000" base units
  charge: "on-success",                     // or "upfront" (the default)
  expectedDurationSeconds: 1,               // required for on-success; at most maxTimeoutSeconds / 2
  capacity: { concurrency: 4, maxQueued: 100, maxQueueWaitSeconds: 60 },   // these are the defaults
  inputSchema: { type: "object", required: ["text"], properties: { text: { type: "string", maxLength: 20000 } } },
  outputSchema: { type: "object", required: ["words"], properties: { words: { type: "integer" } } },
  handler: async ({ text }: { text: string }, { signal }) => ({ words: text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length }),
});

const provider = createProvider({
  baseUrl: "https://api.example.com",       // https only; http://localhost needs dev: true
  network: "stellar:testnet",
  payTo: "G...",                            // public address with a USDC trustline. Never a secret key.
  facilitator: "https://x402.org/facilitator",
  provider: { name: "Example provider" },
  services: [textStats],
  // optional: maxTimeoutSeconds (30–300, default 60), retentionSeconds, holdSeconds (0–30), store,
  //           rateLimit: { requests, windowSeconds, key: (request) => string | undefined }, dev
});

// Mount provider.fetch(request) on any Fetch API server. Hono: app.all("*", (c) => provider.fetch(c.req.raw)).
```

The kit implements §3–§12: the manifest, the challenge, the processing order, jobs, capacity and errors. A handler
receives only the parsed input and an `AbortSignal`, never payment data. Throw to fail the job. Error messages are
not passed on to the client `[E2]`.

Pass `store: sqliteStore(path)` in production. The default `memoryStore()` loses jobs on restart. With SQLite,
paid jobs survive restarts, and processes on one machine share one queue
([kit README](../../packages/provider-kit/README.md#restarts-several-processes-separate-workers)). For an existing
API, gateway mode (`provider-kit serve --config <file>`) does all of this from a JSON config.

## 3. Constants

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `standard` | `stellar-agent-services/provider@1` |
| Default manifest path | `/.well-known/stellar-agent-services.json` |
| Manifest size | ≤ 256 KiB, I-JSON (RFC 7493) |
| Services per manifest | 1–25 |
| Service name | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` |
| `inputSchema` / `outputSchema` | JSON Schema 2020-12, root `"type": "object"`, each ≤ 32 KiB as canonical JSON |
| `maxInputBytes` | default 1,048,576, maximum 10,485,760 |
| `examples` / `tags` | ≤ 5 / ≤ 10, tag pattern `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$` |
| `price.amount` | `^[1-9][0-9]{0,37}$`, USDC base units, 7 decimals (`"100000"` = 0.01 USDC) |
| `maxTimeoutSeconds` | 30–300 |
| `jobs.retentionSeconds` | default 86400, minimum 3600 |
| Networks (CAIP-2) | `stellar:testnet`, `stellar:pubnet` |
| USDC asset, testnet | `CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA` |
| USDC asset, pubnet | `CCW67TSZV3SSS2HXMBQ5JFGCKJNXKZM7UQUWUZPUTHXSTZLEO7SJMI75` |
| `Idempotency-Key` (job id) | lowercase UUID: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |
| `Job-Token` | 32 random bytes, base64url without padding: `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$` |
| create-job hold | ≤ 30 s, then `202` |
| `Retry-After` | whole seconds; `202` responses use 1–60 |
| Problem `type` | `https://algorialabs.github.io/stellar-agent-services/provider/1#error-<code>` (provisional) |

## 4. Manifest

Required: `standard`, `provider.name`, `baseUrl`, `payment`, `services[]`, and for each service `name`,
`description`, `price.amount`, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema`. `expectedDurationSeconds` is required when
`charge` is `on-success`.

Minimal valid manifest (from `test-vectors/manifests.json`, base `minimal`):

```json
{
  "standard": "stellar-agent-services/provider@1",
  "provider": { "name": "Minimal Provider" },
  "baseUrl": "https://minimal.example.com",
  "payment": {
    "protocol": "x402",
    "x402Version": 2,
    "accepts": [
      {
        "scheme": "exact",
        "network": "stellar:testnet",
        "asset": "CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA",
        "payTo": "GBZSBASBFMV5RGKPRIPCB5QQVAJ35IXKMTF2A2766MOA4ZHQ7MLSIPXU",
        "maxTimeoutSeconds": 60,
        "extra": { "areFeesSponsored": true }
      }
    ]
  },
  "services": [
    {
      "name": "echo",
      "description": "Returns its input unchanged. Useful for testing a client.",
      "price": { "amount": "1" },
      "inputSchema": { "type": "object" },
      "outputSchema": { "type": "object" }
    }
  ]
}
```

Optional fields:
- `provider`: `description`, `homepage`, `agentId` (u32), `termsUrl`, `dataUse.storesInputs`,
  `dataUse.trainsOnInputs`
- top level: `jobs.retentionSeconds`
- per service: `title`, `charge` (default `upfront`), `expectedDurationSeconds`, `examples`, `maxInputBytes`,
  `tags`, `capacity.concurrency` (≥ 1), `capacity.maxQueueWaitSeconds` (≥ 0)
- top level and per service: `extensions`

Serving and validating it:
- Serve it over HTTPS with status `200` and `Content-Type: application/json` `[M1]`, and SHOULD send
  `Cache-Control: max-age` of 300 or less `[M4]`.
- `baseUrl` is HTTPS, has the manifest's origin, and has no user info, query, fragment, empty path segment or
  trailing slash `[M5]`.
- Every URL is HTTPS, at most 300 characters, without user info. Loopback `http://` is allowed only in a dev mode
  `[M6]`.
- Validate in three steps: fetch rules `[M1] [M3]`, then the JSON Schema
  ([manifest.schema.json](../../packages/protocol/schemas/manifest.schema.json)) `[M9]`, then the rules the
  schema can't express (`checkManifestRules()`): M1, M3, M5, M7, S6, S9, P11.
- Descriptions say what the service does, when to use it, and its limits. They contain no prices, URLs or
  instructions to the agent (§3.4).
- Schemas use the portable subset: `type properties required additionalProperties items enum const minimum maximum
  minLength maxLength minItems maxItems pattern format title description default examples anyOf $defs` with local
  `$ref`. Avoid `if/then/else`, `patternProperties`, and `oneOf`/`allOf` at the root `[S7]`. Pass large media as
  HTTPS URLs (`"format": "uri"`). URLs in an output stay valid for `retentionSeconds` `[S8]`.

## 5. Endpoints and headers

| Operation | Request | Auth | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| manifest | `GET <manifest URL>` | none | manifest |
| create-job | `POST {baseUrl}/services/{name}/jobs`, body = the input object, `Content-Type: application/json` | x402 payment | job view, `402`, or a problem |
| check-status | `GET {baseUrl}/jobs/{jobId}` | `Job-Token` | job view without `output` |
| get-result | `GET {baseUrl}/jobs/{jobId}/result` | `Job-Token` | job view with `output` when succeeded |

| Header | Direction | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Idempotency-Key` | client → provider | The job id. Send both it and `Job-Token`, or neither `[J1]`. |
| `Job-Token` | client → provider | Bearer secret for the job `[J3]` |
| `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` | provider → client | base64 x402 v2 `PaymentRequired`, on `402` `[P3]` |
| `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` | client → provider | base64 x402 v2 `PaymentPayload` |
| `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` | provider → client | base64 x402 `SettleResponse`, on the response that settled `[P10]` |
| `Location` | provider → client | `{baseUrl}/jobs/{jobId}` on a create-job `202` |
| `Retry-After` | provider → client | Whole seconds, on `202`, `409`, `429` and `503` |

CORS `[J17]` (SHOULD), on the manifest and all three endpoints:
- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`
- `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: PAYMENT-REQUIRED, PAYMENT-RESPONSE, Location, Retry-After`
- `OPTIONS` preflight: `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST` and
  `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Idempotency-Key, Job-Token, PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`

## 6. create-job algorithm (provider)

Follow this order exactly `[§5.4]`. The first failing step answers.

```
POST {baseUrl}/services/{name}/jobs
 1. Headers and body
    - only one of Idempotency-Key / Job-Token        → 400 invalid_request
    - malformed Idempotency-Key or Job-Token          → 400 invalid_request
    - Content-Type is not application/json            → 400 invalid_request
    - body larger than maxInputBytes                  → 413 payload_too_large
                                                        (the service's limit; apply the 10 MiB cap before the lookup)
    - body is not valid UTF-8 JSON                    → 400 invalid_request
    - body is not a JSON object                       → 400 invalid_input
 2. Unknown service                                   → 404 service_not_found
 3. The job id exists [J5–J7]
    - other binding hash or other token               → 422 idempotency_key_reused
    - still being claimed, verified or settled        → 409 request_in_progress + Retry-After
    - otherwise                                       → the existing job view (200/202). No new 402.
                                                        Never settle a payment sent with it.
 4. Input fails inputSchema                           → 400 invalid_input, errors[] = [{ pointer, message }]
 5. Capacity [P8][Q1–Q3]
    - caller over its rate limit                      → 429 rate_limited + Retry-After
    - no slot and no room in the queue                → 503 unavailable + Retry-After
 6. No PAYMENT-SIGNATURE                              → 402 + PAYMENT-REQUIRED (§7)
 7. Decode and verify the payment with the facilitator
    - undecodable, or `accepted` doesn't match        → 402 (x402 error e.g. "invalid_payment")
    - facilitator says invalid                        → 402 (x402 error = its reason)
    - facilitator unreachable                         → 503 unavailable ("nothing was charged")
 8. In ONE atomic step, claim the job id (binding hash, sha256(token)) AND the payment fingerprint [J4][P9]
    - payment fingerprint already used                → 402, x402 error "payment_already_used"
    - an identical request won the race               → that job's view; do not settle [J5]
 9. Settle and run in the order set by `charge` (§8)
10. Respond: wait up to 30 s [J9]
    - job finished                                    → 200 (+ PAYMENT-RESPONSE if this response settled)
    - otherwise                                       → 202 + Location + Retry-After
```

Without `Idempotency-Key` and `Job-Token`, the provider generates both and returns them once, as `jobId` and
`jobToken` in the create-job response `[J2]`.

**Binding hash** `[§5.3]`: `bindingHash = lowercase hex(sha256(JCS({"service": name, "input": input})))`, where JCS
is RFC 8785 canonical JSON. For example, service `text-stats` with input `{"text":"Hello world."}` canonicalizes to
`{"input":{"text":"Hello world."},"service":"text-stats"}` and hashes to
`3d3b3dbdf90621535bd77d1f1d2a1ed0334bf875c7dc7c023caa48cad949ce87`.

**Storage:** keep `jobId`, `service`, `charge`, `bindingHash`, `sha256(Job-Token)` (never the token itself), the
status, timestamps, `output`, `error` and the payment receipt. Make the job id and the payment fingerprint unique
in the same transaction. Compare token hashes in constant time `[J3]`.

## 7. Payment (x402 v2, `exact` scheme on Stellar)

- The manifest has exactly one `payment.accepts` entry, with no `amount` `[P1]`. A `G…` `payTo` has a USDC
  trustline `[P2]` and every `payTo` is a valid strkey `[P11]`. Muxed `M…` addresses are not allowed.
- **Challenge:** the `402` carries a `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header `[P3]` that decodes to:

  ```json
  {
    "x402Version": 2,
    "resource": { "url": "{baseUrl}/services/{name}/jobs", "description": "…", "mimeType": "application/json" },
    "accepts": [{ "scheme": "exact", "network": "…", "asset": "…", "payTo": "…", "amount": "<price.amount>",
                  "maxTimeoutSeconds": 60, "extra": { "areFeesSponsored": true } }]
  }
  ```

  - `accepts` has exactly one entry, equal to the manifest entry plus `amount` = the service's `price.amount` `[P4]`.
  - `resource.url` is the public HTTPS create-job URL `[P5]`.
  - It SHOULD include x402's Bazaar extension `[P6]`.
- **Paid request:** the same request plus `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. Reject a payload whose `x402Version` isn't 2, or
  whose `accepted` differs from the challenge in `scheme`, `network`, `asset`, `amount` or `payTo`.
- **Facilitator:** verify and settle through an x402 facilitator that supports the network with scheme `exact` and
  sponsored fees, such as `https://x402.org/facilitator` on testnet. The provider never signs anything.
- **Settlement outcome:**
  - `settled`: success with a transaction hash.
  - `failed`: only when the facilitator said success is false and gave no transaction.
  - `uncertain`: everything else, including timeouts, 5xx and exceptions. The job becomes `payment_uncertain` and
    is decided later from on-chain data, never by charging again `[J13]`.
- **One payment, one job:** a payment fingerprint is unique `[P9]`.

## 8. Charge policies, states and the job view

| `charge` | Order | If the work fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on-success` | verify → queued → running → work → validate output → settle | Not charged. Settle only if the output matches `outputSchema` `[S1]`. |
| `upfront` | verify → settle → queued → running → work | Charged. v1 has no refunds. |

- `[S2]`: the signed payment expires about `maxTimeoutSeconds` after signing.
  - An `on-success` job whose work and settlement don't finish in time fails, uncharged.
  - Keep `expectedDurationSeconds` ≤ `maxTimeoutSeconds / 2`, and use `upfront` for longer work.

**Transitions** (anything else is forbidden):

```
(new)             → queued | running | payment_uncertain | failed
queued            → running
running           → succeeded | failed | payment_uncertain      (→ payment_uncertain: on-success only)
payment_uncertain → queued | succeeded | failed                 (decided from on-chain data)
succeeded, failed → final [J12]
```

**`charged`:**
- `queued` and `running`: `true` for `upfront`, `false` for `on-success`.
- `succeeded`: `true`.
- `failed`: `true` for `upfront`, except when `error.code` is `payment_failed`; `false` for `on-success`.
- `payment_uncertain`: `"unknown"`.

**Job view** (the body of create-job, check-status and get-result):

```json
{
  "jobId": "0192d3a4-7c1e-7b2a-9f00-3c5e8a1b2c3d",
  "service": "text-stats",
  "status": "queued | running | succeeded | failed | payment_uncertain",
  "charge": "on-success | upfront",
  "charged": true,
  "createdAt": "RFC 3339", "updatedAt": "RFC 3339", "expiresAt": "RFC 3339",
  "output":   { "…": "create-job and get-result, only when succeeded; withheld while payment_uncertain [J14]" },
  "error":    { "type": "…#error-timeout", "title": "…", "code": "service_failed | output_invalid | timeout | payment_failed", "detail": "…" },
  "payment":  { "network": "…", "asset": "…", "amount": "…", "payTo": "…", "payer": "G…", "transaction": "<tx hash>", "settledAt": "RFC 3339" },
  "queue":    { "position": 1, "estimatedStartAt": "RFC 3339" },
  "jobToken": "only in the create-job response, only when the provider generated it [J2]"
}
```

- `error` is present only when `failed`, `payment` only when `charged` is `true`, and `queue` only when `queued`
  `[Q5]`.
- `200` when the job is finished, otherwise `202` with `Retry-After` `[J8]`.
- check-status and get-result never take a payment or cause a charge `[J11]`.
- An unknown job, an expired job, and a missing or wrong token all return the same `404 job_not_found` `[J10]`.
- Jobs stay retrievable for `retentionSeconds` after they finish `[J15]`.

## 9. Capacity and queuing `[§5.8]`

- Check capacity at step 5, before the `402` and before verifying a payment. Check it again on the paid request.
  - `503 unavailable`: the service is full.
  - `429 rate_limited`: this caller sent too many requests.
  - Both carry `Retry-After`, and neither charges anything `[Q1] [Q3]`.
- Admit a job only if it should start within `capacity.maxQueueWaitSeconds`. For `on-success`, it must also finish
  work and settlement before the payment expires `[Q2]`.
- An accepted job is not failed because of load.
  - It waits as `queued`, and a paid `upfront` job SHOULD survive a restart.
  - An `on-success` job that can't start before its payment expires goes `running` → `failed` with `timeout`,
    uncharged `[Q4]`.
- Report the queue in the job view: `"queue": { "position": 1, "estimatedStartAt": "…" }`. Position 1 starts next
  `[Q5]`.
- A `202`'s `Retry-After` reflects when the job will likely change, 1–60 s `[Q6]`.
- Never apply capacity limits to check-status or get-result `[Q7]`.
- Reference admission rule, as in the kit:
  - A service has `concurrency` slots, and `ahead = running + admitted-but-unclaimed + waiting`.
  - When `ahead < concurrency`, the job starts now.
  - Otherwise `position = ahead − concurrency + 1` and `wait = ceil(position / concurrency) × average job seconds`.
    Reject when `position > maxQueued` or `wait > maxQueueWaitSeconds`.

## 10. Errors

Every error other than `402` is RFC 9457, sent as `Content-Type: application/problem+json`:

```json
{ "type": "https://algorialabs.github.io/stellar-agent-services/provider/1#error-invalid_input",
  "title": "Input does not match the service's inputSchema", "status": 400, "code": "invalid_input",
  "detail": "optional, written by the provider", "errors": [{ "pointer": "/text", "message": "must be a string" }] }
```

| `code` | HTTP | When | `Retry-After` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | 400 | Malformed JSON, wrong content type, bad header, or only one of `Idempotency-Key` / `Job-Token` | |
| `invalid_input` | 400 | Input fails `inputSchema`; `errors[]` has JSON Pointers | |
| `service_not_found` | 404 | No such service | |
| `job_not_found` | 404 | Unknown or expired job, or a wrong or missing token | |
| `request_in_progress` | 409 | The job id is being claimed, verified or settled `[J7]` | yes |
| `payload_too_large` | 413 | Body over `maxInputBytes` | |
| `idempotency_key_reused` | 422 | Same job id, different request `[J6]` | |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | This caller sent too many requests `[Q1]` | yes |
| `unavailable` | 503 | At capacity, or a dependency is down | yes |

- Job failure codes, in the job view's `error.code`: `service_failed`, `output_invalid`, `timeout` and
  `payment_failed`. A failed job's `error` has no `status`.
- `[E1]` Clients act on `code`, never on `title` or `detail`.
- `[E2]` Problems never contain request headers, payment payloads or job tokens. Never copy a handler's exception
  message into `detail`.

## 11. Identity (Stellar 8004)

- `[I1]` The provider's 8004 registration file lists
  `{ "name": "stellar-agent-services", "endpoint": "<manifest URL>", "version": "1" }` in `services`. It SHOULD
  also list `{ "name": "web", "endpoint": "<baseUrl>" }` and set the `x402` flag.
- `[I2]` `provider.agentId` in the manifest is that registration's id.
- `[I3]` The manifest's `payTo` equals `get_agent_wallet(agentId)` on chain.
- Registration and validation requests are owner actions. They run offline and sign through the Stellar CLI
  keychain, never in the provider runtime: `provider-kit register`, then `provider-kit request-validation
  --validator <verifier G…> --source <key>`, which works for any provider with `--manifest <url>`.
- A validation request's `request_hash` is the SHA-256 of its document's canonical JSON, and its `request_uri` holds
  exactly those bytes ([verification.md](../verification.md#stellar-8004-validation-registry)). The validator is never
  the agent's owner or wallet.

## 12. Security invariants (provider)

- No Stellar secret key in the runtime, config, environment or logs.
- Store `sha256(Job-Token)` only, and compare in constant time.
- A `404` never reveals whether a job exists.
- One payment buys at most one job. A repeated request never settles again.
- An uncertain settlement is never retried with a new charge.
- Schemas never reference remote documents `[S5]`.
- Output is validated before settling (`on-success`) and before storing.
- Problems and logs sent to clients never echo headers, payment payloads or tokens.
- `description`, `title` and `examples` are untrusted text for clients. Write them as plain descriptions, not as
  instructions.

## 13. Testing and conformance

**Test vectors** in [packages/protocol/test-vectors](../../packages/protocol/test-vectors). Each file explains
itself in its `description`.

| File | Pins |
| --- | --- |
| `manifests.json` | Manifest validation: JSON Schema cases and code-rule cases, as RFC 6902 patches to a base |
| `challenges.json` | `checkChallenge`: a `402` versus the approved manifest `[P3–P5]` |
| `canonical-json.json` | RFC 8785 output, including number formatting |
| `binding-hash.json` | Binding hashes `[§5.3]` |
| `headers.json` | `Idempotency-Key` and `Job-Token` patterns, and `Retry-After` parsing |
| `job-states.json` | Allowed transitions and `charged` per status, charge and failure code |
| `problems.json` | Error codes, HTTP statuses and which ones carry `Retry-After` |
| `validation-requests.json` | Validation request documents: canonical bytes, `request_hash` and the `data:` URI |

**TypeScript helpers** in `@stellar-agent-services/protocol`, which has no runtime dependencies:
`checkManifestRules`, `checkChallenge`, `canonicalJson`, `canonicalSha256`, `bindingHash`, `canTransition`,
`chargedFor`, `jobViewHttpStatus`, `parseRetryAfter`, `problem`, `jobError`, `createJobUrl`, `jobStatusUrl`,
`jobResultUrl`, `stellarAddressKind`, `validationRequestHash`, `validationRequestDataUri`, `USDC_ASSET`.

**A real paid call on testnet** against a local provider, using the payment client CLI (see
[packages/payment-client/README.md](../../packages/payment-client/README.md)):

```bash
npx stellar-pay wallet create
npx stellar-pay wallet fund --usdc 2
npx stellar-pay pay http://localhost:8787/.well-known/stellar-agent-services.json text-stats '{"text":"Hello agents."}' --dev
```

**Acceptance checklist for a provider:**
- [ ] The manifest passes the JSON Schema and `checkManifestRules` with no violations.
- [ ] Invalid input returns `400 invalid_input` and never a `402`.
- [ ] An unpaid valid request returns a `402` whose challenge passes `checkChallenge`.
- [ ] A paid request returns `200`/`202`, and the job view's `payment.transaction` is a real transfer to `payTo`.
- [ ] Repeating the paid request (same id, token and input) returns the same job, with exactly one transfer on
  chain.
- [ ] The same id with another input returns `422`. A wrong token returns `404`.
- [ ] A facilitator timeout during settlement gives `payment_uncertain`, not `failed`.
- [ ] A burst of 20 simultaneous requests gets only `402`, `429` or `503` with `Retry-After`. No `500`, no
  timeout.
- [ ] check-status and get-result work while the service is at capacity.
- [ ] CORS headers are present, including on `OPTIONS`.

**Conformance levels** `[§8]`:
- **1 Described:** C1 manifest + C6 hygiene.
- **2 Payable:** + C3 challenge + C4 paid call.
- **3 Recoverable:** + C5 recovery.
- Independent of the levels: **Registered** (C2 identity + a Validation Registry record) and **Load-safe** (C7
  load).
- The checks are defined in [verification.md](../verification.md). Run them with
  `node packages/verifier/dist/cli/index.js check <manifest-url>` (`--dev` for `http://localhost`): every check that
  needs no payment. Exit code 0 means every check that ran passed; each failure names its rule id.

## 14. Client rules (agents, wallets, apps)

- Fetch the manifest with no redirects, at most 256 KiB, as I-JSON `[M3]`.
  - Ignore unknown fields, and reject another major `standard` `[M8]`.
  - Never fetch remote schemas `[S5]`.
- Before the first request, generate and **persist** a UUID job id and a 32-byte token `[J1]`. Recovery depends on
  them.
- Unpaid create-job → `402`. Compare the challenge with the approved manifest, and refuse to sign on any mismatch
  `[P7]`.
  - Show the price, recipient, network and `charge` before approval `[S3]`.
- Sign once. Send the paid request with the same id, token and input.
- `429` / `503` from create-job: wait `Retry-After` plus jitter, then send the identical request again `[Q8]`.
  - On a paid request, send the same `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`.
  - Stop before the payment expires, and give up after a bounded wait.
  - The user was not charged.
- `202`: poll check-status or get-result no faster than `Retry-After`. A `429` or `503` while polling means "later"
  `[Q9]`. Use an HTTP timeout above 30 s `[J9]`.
- Lost response, crash or timeout after sending payment: recover with get-result. **Never sign or pay again** for
  that job.
- `payment_uncertain`: stop polling and tell the user not to pay again. Only the provider resolves it `[J13]`.
- Show "paid" only after confirming the transaction on chain against what the user approved, not against the
  receipt. One transaction proves one job `[J16]`.
- Label `description`, `title` and `examples` as provider-supplied when you show them to an LLM (§10 of the spec).
- Map each service 1:1 to an MCP tool with `name`, `title`, `description`, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema`. Keep
  price, network and `charge` out of the tool definition (Appendix B).

## 15. Common mistakes

| Mistake | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Answering `402` before validating input or checking capacity | P8, Q1 |
| `amount` in the manifest's payment option, or more than one `accepts` entry | P1 |
| `baseUrl` with a trailing slash, or on another origin than the manifest | M5 |
| Settling again when a known job id is repeated | J5 |
| Deriving the job id from the input instead of `Idempotency-Key` | J4 |
| Different responses for "unknown job" and "wrong token" | J10 |
| Storing the raw `Job-Token` | J3 |
| Echoing headers, payment payloads, tokens or exception messages in errors | E2 |
| Marking a facilitator timeout as `failed`, or settling again | J13 |
| Long `on-success` work (more than `maxTimeoutSeconds / 2`) | S2 |
| `500`, a dropped connection or a hang under load instead of `503` + `Retry-After` | Q1 |
| Rate-limiting check-status or get-result | Q7 |
| `Retry-After` as a decimal, or missing on `409`, `429` or `503` | §6, Q1 |
| Holding create-job open longer than 30 s | J9 |
| CORS without `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`, so browsers can't read `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` | J17 |
| A non-object schema root, or a remote `$ref` | S4, S5 |
| Price, URLs or agent instructions in `description` | §3.4 |
| Changing a finished job | J12 |
| A muxed `M…` `payTo` | P11, §4.1 |

## 16. Rule index

Manifest:
- **M1** The manifest is served over HTTPS, `200`, `application/json`.
- **M2** Any URL. The default is `/.well-known/stellar-agent-services.json`, and the 8004 registration points to
  the actual URL.
- **M3** Clients don't follow redirects. At most 256 KiB, I-JSON.
- **M4** SHOULD send `Cache-Control: max-age` ≤ 300.
- **M5** `baseUrl` is HTTPS on the manifest's origin, with no user info, query, fragment, empty segment or trailing
  `/`.
- **M6** URLs are HTTPS, ≤ 300 characters, without user info. Loopback `http://` only in dev mode.
- **M7** Service names are unique.
- **M8** Clients ignore unknown fields and reject another major `standard`.
- **M9** The manifest is valid against the JSON Schema.

Services:
- **S1** `on-success` settles only for output that is valid against `outputSchema`.
- **S2** A payment expires about `maxTimeoutSeconds` after signing; overrunning `on-success` work fails uncharged.
  SHOULD keep the expected duration ≤ half of it.
- **S3** Clients show `charge` before approval.
- **S4** Schema roots are `"type": "object"`.
- **S5** No external `$ref` or `$dynamicRef`; `$schema` is 2020-12 only; clients never fetch remote schemas.
- **S6** Each schema is ≤ 32 KiB as canonical JSON.
- **S7** SHOULD use the portable JSON Schema subset.
- **S8** URLs in an output stay valid for `retentionSeconds`.
- **S9** Examples validate against their schemas.

Payment:
